5.text: Another tale mentions the country Luᵋˊren, which is situated on the

6.text: seashore. This country is mentioned in several tales as one of the countries

7.text: of the time of the first creation.² The tale says that the Maritime people living

8.text: in that country were exterminated by famine. Only two were left, — a full-

9.text: grown girl and her infant brother. She fed him with pounded meat. When

10.text: he grew up, she asked him to marry her. “Otherwise we shall remain child-

11.text: less,” said the sister. “We shall have no descendants, and the earth will

12.text: remain without people. It cannot be peopled otherwise. And who sees us?

13.text: Who will say, ‘Shame’? Who will know about it in the world? We are all

14.text: alone in the world.” The brother said, “I do not know. I feel bad. It is

15.text: forbidden.” Then the sister began to think, “How can I do it? Our line of

16.text: descent will break off with us.”

17.text: Then follows a very vivid and detailed description of how the young

18.text: woman goes to a distant place, builds a house, quite different from their own,

19.text: prepares everything belonging to it, and how she makes new clothes for her-

20.text: self. Then she returns and tells the brother that she has seen a house some-

21.text: where on the shore. The brother goes in search of this house and finds it.

22.text: The sister is already there. She has changed her clothes, the expression of

23.text: her face, the tone of her voice, and he takes her for another woman. After

24.text: some hesitation, he takes her for his wife. Then begins a life in two houses:

25.text: the sister is here and there, and plays with success her double role. Finally,

26.text: when she is pregnant, the brother ceases to think of his sister, and they live

27.text: at the new place. One child is born, then another. The family multiplies

28.text: and becomes a people. From them are born all the people in the camps

30.text: Most of the marriages between relatives are concluded at a tender age,

31.text: sometimes when the bridegroom and the bride are still infants. The marriage

32.text: ritual is performed, and the children grow up, playing together. When a

33.text: little older, they tend the herd together. Of course, the ties between them

34.text: grow to be very strong, often stronger even than death: when one dies, the

35.text: other also dies from grief, or commits suicide.

36.text: Similar to these marriages are those between the members of families

37.text: friendly to each other, though not connected by ties of blood. Sometimes

38.text: such families agree to a marriage between their children even before the

39.text: children are born. Thus, when I was on the Dry Anui River, two men of
